gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-inter-tight: Inter Tight keeps its lowercase compact, with short ascenders and curve tails pulled back, like tubing bent into tidy shapes. Nulshock stretches wide above it, outlined and bold.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-karla: Stretched wide with generous tracking, Nulshock draws every stroke in a single unshaded outline, technical and bold. Karla follows with a gaping c and a tall middle band, so long paragraphs look stocky and friendly.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-kedebideri: Flat, stencil-cut and stretched out, Nulshock looks like it was punched from sheet metal. Kedebideri answers with a skyward x-height and rounded, inviting letters, which is the pair's whole appeal: rigid on top, friendly below.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-khula: Bent pipe cleaner, stretched wide: that is Nulshock, with capitals barely taller than its lowercase. Khula brings a tall midsection and curves that hold their mouths open, a loosely drawn counterweight to the rigid heading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-krub: Nulshock is stretched wide, every stroke cut to a single width. Krub sits beneath it with a pronounced x-height and curves that lift off before closing, giving the heading's rigid outline a looser, plain sans partner.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-kufam: Wide, technical and outlined like a neon tube, Nulshock sets a bold tone while Kufam holds the line below with big bodies and hardly any ascenders. Text in it feels clean and contemporary.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend: Lexend has outsized lowercase, open jaws on every curve and a thickness that holds steady around bends. Nulshock handles the loud technical stretch of a bold outline, while the plain sans handles approachable reading.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-lexend-deca: Nulshock is stretched, spacious and outlined in a single bold line. Lexend Deca takes over below with a plain sans line that never swells, small capitals beside big lowercase, and terminals that stop short of curling back.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-liter: Liter has no stroke contrast whatsoever and lowercase with great vertical presence. Over many lines the sans feels modern and clear, with wide mouths on round forms, while Nulshock's wide outline stays up top.
gen-dafont-nulshock-gf-mada: Wide and technical, Nulshock cuts stems and curves from one gauge of tubing. Mada follows with curves that refuse to close and a towering midzone, so the heading handles the bold statement and the sans handles approachable reading.
